meta.topic: 线性代数：内积与正交化、二次型标准形、正定性与惯性定理、特征值变分、对偶与双线性型、商空间、张量积

zh: 在 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 中定义 $(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha^{T}\beta=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_ib_i$。它满足双线性、对称性与正定性：$(\alpha,\alpha)=\sum_i a_i^2\ge0$，且等号成立当且仅当 $\alpha=0$。因此可定义范数 $\|\alpha\|=\sqrt{(\alpha,\alpha)}$，只有 $\alpha\ne0$ 时才能单位化；正交定义为 $(\alpha,\beta)=0$。由 Cauchy–Schwarz 不等式 $|(\alpha,\beta)|\le\|\alpha\|\,\|\beta\|$，夹角 $\cos\theta=\dfrac{(\alpha,\beta)}{\|\alpha\|\,\|\beta\|}$ 才有定义。

设 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ 两两正交且都非零。若 $\sum_{k=1}^{m}c_k\alpha_k=0$，对固定的 $j$ 两边取与 $\alpha_j$ 的内积，交叉项因正交性全部消失，只剩 $c_j(\alpha_j,\alpha_j)=0$。由 $\alpha_j\ne0$ 得 $(\alpha_j,\alpha_j)>0$，故 $c_j=0$。由于 $j$ 任意，所有系数为零，所以该正交组线性无关。非零条件不能去掉：含零向量的正交组必定线性相关。

设 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ 线性无关。令 $\beta_1=\alpha_1$，并归纳假定 $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}$ 两两正交、非零，且 $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}=\operatorname{span}\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1}\}$。定义 $$\beta_i=\alpha_i-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\frac{(\alpha_i,\beta_j)}{(\beta_j,\beta_j)}\beta_j.$$ 对每个 $k<i$，用 $(\cdot,\beta_k)$ 作用；由正交性，除第 $k$ 项外其余项全为零，于是 $$\begin{aligned}(\beta_i,\beta_k)&=(\alpha_i,\beta_k)\\&\quad-\frac{(\alpha_i,\beta_k)}{(\beta_k,\beta_k)}(\beta_k,\beta_k)\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$ 分母 $(\beta_j,\beta_j)>0$，故上述定义合法。

还需说明 $\beta_i\ne0$。若 $\beta_i=0$，则 $\alpha_i=\sum_{j<i}\dfrac{(\alpha_i,\beta_j)}{(\beta_j,\beta_j)}\beta_j\in\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}$。由归纳假设 $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}=\operatorname{span}\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1}\}$，这与 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_i$ 线性无关矛盾。故 $\beta_i\ne0$。又 $\beta_i$ 与 $\alpha_i$ 只相差 $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}$ 的线性组合，所以 $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_i\}=\operatorname{span}\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_i\}$，归纳可以继续。

最后单位化 $\eta_i=\beta_i/\|\beta_i\|$，得到与 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ 张成同一子空间的标准正交组。若 $m=n$，它就是 $\mathbb{R}^n$ 的标准正交基。此时任意 $x=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\eta_i$ 满足 $(\eta_j,x)=c_j(\eta_j,\eta_j)=c_j$，所以 $$x=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(\eta_j^{T}x)\eta_j.$$ 把 $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$ 按列排成 $Q$，正交列给出 $Q^{T}Q=E$，从而 $Q^{-1}=Q^{T}$，且 $QQ^{T}=E$，上式正是 $x=QQ^{T}x$。

条件核查：若 $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ 线性相关，施密特过程必在某个 $i$ 处产生 $\beta_i=0$，单位化随即失败。例如 $\alpha_2=2\alpha_1$ 时，$\beta_2=\alpha_2-\dfrac{2(\alpha_1,\alpha_1)}{(\alpha_1,\alpha_1)}\alpha_1=0$。所以「线性无关」是前提而不是结论。几何上，$\beta_i$ 是 $\alpha_i$ 减去它在 $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}$ 上的正交投影后的余量，因而与整个前面的子空间正交。
en: On $\mathbb{R}^n$ define $(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha^{T}\beta=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_ib_i$. It is bilinear, symmetric and positive definite: $(\alpha,\alpha)=\sum_i a_i^2\ge0$, with equality iff $\alpha=0$. Hence the norm $\|\alpha\|=\sqrt{(\alpha,\alpha)}$ is defined, and only a nonzero vector can be normalized; orthogonality means $(\alpha,\beta)=0$. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality $|(\alpha,\beta)|\le\|\alpha\|\,\|\beta\|$ is what makes the angle $\cos\theta=\dfrac{(\alpha,\beta)}{\|\alpha\|\,\|\beta\|}$ well defined.

Let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ be pairwise orthogonal and nonzero. If $\sum_{k=1}^{m}c_k\alpha_k=0$, take the inner product of both sides with a fixed $\alpha_j$; all cross terms vanish by orthogonality, leaving $c_j(\alpha_j,\alpha_j)=0$. Since $\alpha_j\ne0$ gives $(\alpha_j,\alpha_j)>0$, we get $c_j=0$. As $j$ is arbitrary, all coefficients vanish, so the orthogonal set is linearly independent. The nonzero hypothesis is essential: an orthogonal set containing $0$ is necessarily linearly dependent.

Let $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ be linearly independent. Put $\beta_1=\alpha_1$, and assume inductively that $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}$ are pairwise orthogonal, nonzero, and satisfy $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}=\operatorname{span}\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1}\}$. Define $$\beta_i=\alpha_i-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\frac{(\alpha_i,\beta_j)}{(\beta_j,\beta_j)}\beta_j.$$ For each $k<i$, take the inner product with $\beta_k$; by orthogonality every term except the $k$-th one vanishes, so $$\begin{aligned}(\beta_i,\beta_k)&=(\alpha_i,\beta_k)\\&\quad-\frac{(\alpha_i,\beta_k)}{(\beta_k,\beta_k)}(\beta_k,\beta_k)\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$ The denominators $(\beta_j,\beta_j)$ are positive, so the definition is legitimate.

We must also show $\beta_i\ne0$. If $\beta_i=0$, then $\alpha_i=\sum_{j<i}\dfrac{(\alpha_i,\beta_j)}{(\beta_j,\beta_j)}\beta_j\in\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}$. By the induction hypothesis this span equals $\operatorname{span}\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1}\}$, contradicting the linear independence of $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_i$. Hence $\beta_i\ne0$. Moreover, $\beta_i$ differs from $\alpha_i$ only by a linear combination of $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}$, so $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_i\}=\operatorname{span}\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_i\}$ and the induction continues.

Finally normalize $\eta_i=\beta_i/\|\beta_i\|$; the result is an orthonormal set spanning the same subspace as $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$. If $m=n$, it is an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$. For $x=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\eta_i$, taking the inner product with $\eta_j$ gives $(\eta_j,x)=c_j(\eta_j,\eta_j)=c_j$, hence $$x=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(\eta_j^{T}x)\eta_j.$$ Placing $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$ as the columns of $Q$, the orthonormal columns give $Q^{T}Q=E$, so $Q^{-1}=Q^{T}$ and $QQ^{T}=E$; the displayed formula is exactly $x=QQ^{T}x$.

Hypothesis check: if $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ are linearly dependent, Gram–Schmidt must produce $\beta_i=0$ at some stage, and normalization fails immediately. For example, if $\alpha_2=2\alpha_1$, then $\beta_2=\alpha_2-\dfrac{2(\alpha_1,\alpha_1)}{(\alpha_1,\alpha_1)}\alpha_1=0$. Thus linear independence is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. Geometrically, $\beta_i$ is the residual of $\alpha_i$ after subtracting its orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}\{\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{i-1}\}$, so it is orthogonal to that entire subspace.

zh: 设 $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\sum_{1\le i\le j\le n}c_{ij}x_ix_j$。令 $a_{ii}=c_{ii}$，并对 $i<j$ 令 $a_{ij}=a_{ji}=\frac12c_{ij}$，则 $f=x^{T}Ax$ 且 $A^{T}=A$。反过来，从任意矩阵 $B$ 出发，$x^{T}Bx$ 是标量，故 $x^{T}Bx=(x^{T}Bx)^{T}=x^{T}B^{T}x$，于是 $x^{T}Bx=x^{T}\frac{B+B^{T}}2x$；所以总可取对称矩阵，且它由 $a_{ij}=\frac12\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}$ 唯一确定。在要求 $A$ 对称的前提下，交叉项系数必须平分，不能整块放在 $a_{ij}$。

作可逆线性变换 $x=Py$（$P$ 可逆），则 $$f=x^{T}Ax=(Py)^{T}A(Py)=y^{T}(P^{T}AP)y.$$ 新矩阵 $P^{T}AP$ 仍对称，因为 $(P^{T}AP)^{T}=P^{T}A^{T}P=P^{T}AP$。又 $\operatorname{rank}(P^{T}AP)=\operatorname{rank}(A)$：左乘或右乘可逆矩阵都不改变秩。故合同变换保持二次型的秩，但一般改变特征值（保持特征值的是相似变换）。例如 $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)$、$P=\operatorname{diag}(1,\frac12)$ 时，$P^{T}AP=\operatorname{diag}(1,1)$。

正交变换法：$A$ 实对称，由谱定理存在正交矩阵 $Q$（$Q^{T}Q=E$）使 $$Q^{T}AQ=\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n).$$ 令 $x=Qy$，则 $f=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2$。这里 $Q^{-1}=Q^{T}$，所以合同与相似同时发生；标准形的系数恰为特征值，且 $\|x\|=\|Qy\|=\|y\|$，变换只是旋转或反射。

两条路径给出的标准形可以不同：正交变换给 $\sum\lambda_iy_i^2$，配方法给 $\sum d_iz_i^2$，系数一般不相等。但两者由可逆变换互相联系，故秩相同；由惯性定理，正、负平方项的个数 $(p,q)$ 也相同，并且都能进一步化为规范形 $$z_1^2+\cdots+z_p^2-z_{p+1}^2-\cdots-z_r^2,\qquad r=p+q=\operatorname{rank}(A).$$ 所以标准形不唯一，正、负惯性指数唯一；合同保持秩与惯性指数，但不保持特征值。
en: Let $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\sum_{1\le i\le j\le n}c_{ij}x_ix_j$. Set $a_{ii}=c_{ii}$ and, for $i<j$, $a_{ij}=a_{ji}=\frac12c_{ij}$; then $f=x^{T}Ax$ with $A^{T}=A$. Conversely, starting from any matrix $B$, the scalar $x^{T}Bx$ equals its transpose $x^{T}B^{T}x$, so $x^{T}Bx=x^{T}\frac{B+B^{T}}2x$; hence a symmetric matrix may always be used, and it is uniquely determined by $a_{ij}=\frac12\frac{\partial^2f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}$. Under the requirement that $A$ be symmetric, a cross-term coefficient must be split equally, not assigned entirely to $a_{ij}$.

For an invertible linear change $x=Py$, $$f=x^{T}Ax=(Py)^{T}A(Py)=y^{T}(P^{T}AP)y.$$ The new matrix $P^{T}AP$ is still symmetric, since $(P^{T}AP)^{T}=P^{T}A^{T}P=P^{T}AP$. Also $\operatorname{rank}(P^{T}AP)=\operatorname{rank}(A)$, because multiplication by an invertible matrix on either side preserves rank. Thus congruence preserves the rank of the form but generally changes eigenvalues (similarity, not congruence, preserves them): for $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)$ and $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,\frac12)$, $P^{T}AP=\operatorname{diag}(1,1)$.

Orthogonal method: since $A$ is real symmetric, the spectral theorem gives an orthogonal $Q$ ($Q^{T}Q=E$) with $$Q^{T}AQ=\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n).$$ Setting $x=Qy$ yields $f=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2$. Here $Q^{-1}=Q^{T}$, so congruence and similarity occur simultaneously; the coefficients are exactly the eigenvalues, and $\|x\|=\|Qy\|=\|y\|$, so the change is only a rotation or reflection.

e i)$ has all diagonal entries equal to $1$, with off-diagonal entries only in row $i$; its determinant is $1$, so it is invertible. Repeat on the remaining variables; if at some stage all square coefficients vanish while the remaining form is nonzero, use the substitution of Step 5. The result is $f=\sum d_iy_i^2$, and the number of nonzero $d_i$ equals the rank.

e0$. Then $$2a_{ij}x_ix_j=2a_{ij}(y_i^2-y_j^2),$$ which creates nonzero square terms, and we return to the previous step. For example, $f=2x_1x_2$ becomes $2y_1^2-2y_2^2$ under this substitution.

The two routes may produce different canonical forms: the orthogonal method gives $\sum\lambda_iy_i^2$, while completing the square gives $\sum d_iz_i^2$, and the coefficients generally differ. Since the two are related by invertible changes, the rank is the same; by the law of inertia the numbers $(p,q)$ of positive and negative squares are also the same, and both reduce further to the normal form $$z_1^2+\cdots+z_p^2-z_{p+1}^2-\cdots-z_r^2,\qquad r=p+q=\operatorname{rank}(A).$$ Thus a canonical form is not unique, but the inertia indices are; congruence preserves rank and inertia, not eigenvalues.

zh: 设 $A$ 实对称，$f(x)=x^{T}Ax$。若对一切 $x\ne0$ 都有 $f(x)>0$，就称 $A$ 正定。取 $x=e_i$ 得 $a_{ii}=e_i^{T}Ae_i>0$。若 $Ax=0$ 有非零解 $x$，则 $f(x)=x^{T}Ax=0$，与正定性矛盾，故 $A$ 可逆、$|A|\ne0$。注意 $f(0)=0$ 是允许的：正定性只要求非零向量上的值严格为正。

由谱定理写 $A=Q\Lambda Q^{T}$，其中 $Q$ 正交，$\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$。令 $x=Qy$，则 $$f(x)=x^{T}Ax=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2,\qquad \|x\|=\|y\|.$$ 若所有 $\lambda_i>0$，则对 $x
e0$（从而 $y
e0$）有 $f\ge(\min_i\lambda_i)\|y\|^2>0$。反之，若某个 $\lambda_k\le0$，取 $x=Qe_k
e0$，得 $f=\lambda_k\le0$，故不正定。因此 $A$ 正定 $\iff$ 全部特征值 $>0$。

必要性（Sylvester 判据的一半）：设 $A$ 正定，$A_k$ 为其左上角 $k$ 阶顺序主子矩阵。对任意 $0\ne y\in\mathbb{R}^k$，令 $\tilde y=(y,0,\dots,0)^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^n$，则 $y^{T}A_ky=\tilde y^{T}A\tilde y>0$，故 $A_k$ 正定。由第 2 步，$A_k$ 的特征值全为正，于是 $$D_k=\det A_k=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(A_k)>0.$$ 这对 $k=1,\dots,n$ 都成立。

充分性：设 $D_1,\dots,D_n>0$。对对称矩阵作不换行的消元，可得 $$A=LDL^{T},\qquad L\ \text{为单位下三角矩阵},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n),$$ 其中 $d_1=D_1$，$d_k=D_k/D_{k-1}$（$k\ge2$）。这些等式由顺序主子式在消元中的变化直接得到；$D_k>0$ 保证所有 $d_k>0$ 且消元不中断。对 $x\ne0$，$L$ 可逆给出 $L^{T}x\ne0$，于是 $$x^{T}Ax=x^{T}LDL^{T}x=\sum_{k=1}^{n}d_k(L^{T}x)_k^2>0.$$ 故 $A$ 正定。

惯性定理：设同一二次型在两个基下分别化为 $$\begin{aligned}f&=\sum_{i=1}^{p}z_i^2-\sum_{i=p+1}^{p+q}z_i^2\\&=\sum_{i=1}^{p'}w_i^2-\sum_{i=p'+1}^{p'+q'}w_i^2,\end{aligned}$$ 其中 $r=p+q=p'+q'=\operatorname{rank}(A)$。若 $p>p'$，取 $U=\{z_{p+1}=\cdots=z_n=0\}$（$\dim U=p$）与 $Z=\{w_1=\cdots=w_{p'}=0\}$（$\dim Z=n-p'$）。因 $\dim U+\dim Z=p+n-p'>n$，存在 $0\ne v\in U\cap Z$。在 $U$ 上 $f\ge0$，在 $Z$ 上 $f\le0$，故 $f(v)=0$；但 $U$ 上 $f=0$ 迫使 $z_1=\cdots=z_p=0$，结合 $U$ 的定义得 $v=0$，矛盾。所以 $p\le p'$；对称地 $p'\le p$，故 $p=p'$，$q=q'$。

由惯性定理，正定等价于 $p=n$（此时 $q=0$），即 $A$ 与 $E$ 合同：存在可逆 $P$ 使 $P^{T}AP=E$。于是 $A=(P^{-1})^{T}P^{-1}$，取 $C=P^{-1}$ 得 $A=C^{T}C$，且 $f=\|Cx\|^2$。反过来，若 $A=C^{T}C$ 且 $C$ 可逆，则 $x\ne0\Rightarrow Cx\ne0\Rightarrow f=\|Cx\|^2>0$。故正定 $\iff A\cong E\iff A=C^{T}C$（$C$ 可逆）。反例：$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ 有 $D_1=1>0$、$D_2=0$，特征值为 $0,2$，$f=(x_1+x_2)^2$ 在直线 $x_1+x_2=0$ 上为零，故只是半正定而非正定。
en: Let $A$ be real symmetric and $f(x)=x^{T}Ax$. If $f(x)>0$ for every $x\ne0$, then $A$ is positive definite. Taking $x=e_i$ gives $a_{ii}=e_i^{T}Ae_i>0$. If $Ax=0$ had a nonzero solution $x$, then $f(x)=x^{T}Ax=0$, contradicting positive definiteness; hence $A$ is invertible and $|A|\ne0$. Note that $f(0)=0$ is allowed: positive definiteness requires strict positivity only on nonzero vectors.

By the spectral theorem write $A=Q\Lambda Q^{T}$ with $Q$ orthogonal and $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$. For $x=Qy$, $$f(x)=x^{T}Ax=y^{T}\Lambda y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_iy_i^2,\qquad \|x\|=\|y\|.$$ If all $\lambda_i>0$, then for $x
e0$ (hence $y
e0$), $f\ge(\min_i\lambda_i)\|y\|^2>0$. Conversely, if some $\lambda_k\le0$, take $x=Qe_k
e0$; then $f=\lambda_k\le0$, so the form is not positive definite. Therefore $A$ is positive definite iff all eigenvalues are positive.

Necessity (one half of Sylvester's criterion): let $A$ be positive definite and let $A_k$ be its top-left $k\times k$ principal submatrix. For any $0\ne y\in\mathbb{R}^k$, put $\tilde y=(y,0,\dots,0)^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^n$; then $y^{T}A_ky=\tilde y^{T}A\tilde y>0$, so $A_k$ is positive definite. By Step 2 all eigenvalues of $A_k$ are positive, hence $$D_k=\det A_k=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(A_k)>0.$$ This holds for every $k=1,\dots,n$.

Sufficiency: assume $D_1,\dots,D_n>0$. Gaussian elimination without row exchanges gives $$A=LDL^{T},\qquad L\ \text{unit lower triangular},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n),$$ where $d_1=D_1$ and $d_k=D_k/D_{k-1}$ for $k\ge2$. These identities follow from how leading principal minors change under elimination; $D_k>0$ ensures every $d_k>0$ and no elimination step breaks down. For $x\ne0$, invertibility of $L$ gives $L^{T}x\ne0$, so $$x^{T}Ax=x^{T}LDL^{T}x=\sum_{k=1}^{n}d_k(L^{T}x)_k^2>0.$$ Hence $A$ is positive definite.

Law of inertia: suppose the same form is reduced in two bases to $$\begin{aligned}f&=\sum_{i=1}^{p}z_i^2-\sum_{i=p+1}^{p+q}z_i^2\\&=\sum_{i=1}^{p'}w_i^2-\sum_{i=p'+1}^{p'+q'}w_i^2,\end{aligned}$$ with $r=p+q=p'+q'=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. If $p>p'$, set $U=\{z_{p+1}=\cdots=z_n=0\}$ (dimension $p$) and $Z=\{w_1=\cdots=w_{p'}=0\}$ (dimension $n-p'$). Since $\dim U+\dim Z=p+n-p'>n$, there is $0\ne v\in U\cap Z$. On $U$ we have $f\ge0$, while on $Z$ we have $f\le0$, so $f(v)=0$. But on $U$, $f=0$ forces $z_1=\cdots=z_p=0$, and with $z_{p+1}=\cdots=z_n=0$ this gives $v=0$, a contradiction. Hence $p\le p'$; symmetrically $p'\le p$, so $p=p'$ and $q=q'$.

By the law of inertia, positive definiteness is exactly $p=n$ (then $q=0$), i.e. $A$ is congruent to $E$: there is an invertible $P$ with $P^{T}AP=E$. Then $A=(P^{-1})^{T}P^{-1}$; setting $C=P^{-1}$ gives $A=C^{T}C$ and $f=\|Cx\|^2$. Conversely, if $A=C^{T}C$ with $C$ invertible, then $x\ne0$ implies $Cx\ne0$, so $f=\|Cx\|^2>0$. Thus positive definite $\iff A\cong E\iff A=C^{T}C$ for some invertible $C$. Counterexample: $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has $D_1=1>0$ and $D_2=0$, eigenvalues $0,2$, and $f=(x_1+x_2)^2$ vanishes on the line $x_1+x_2=0$; it is positive semidefinite but not positive definite.

zh: 设 $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ 为 Hermitian（$A^{H}=A$），特征值按升序排列 $\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n$，并取标准正交特征基 $u_1,\dots,u_n$：$Au_i=\lambda_iu_i$，$u_i^{H}u_j=\delta_{ij}$。对 $x\ne0$ 定义 Rayleigh 商 $$R(x)=\frac{x^{H}Ax}{x^{H}x}.$$ 写 $x=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_iu_i$，则 $x^{H}Ax=\sum_i\lambda_i|c_i|^2$、$x^{H}x=\sum_i|c_i|^2$，所以 $$R(x)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i|c_i|^2}{\sum_i|c_i|^2}.$$ 它是特征值以 $|c_i|^2$ 为权的加权平均，特别地取实值，且 $R(cx)=R(x)$（$c\ne0$）。

由加权平均立刻得到 $\lambda_1\le R(x)\le\lambda_n$。取 $x=u_1$ 得 $R=\lambda_1$，取 $x=u_n$ 得 $R=\lambda_n$，故 $$\lambda_1=\min_{x\ne0}R(x),\qquad \lambda_n=\max_{x\ne0}R(x).$$ 等号条件也可读出：$R(x)=\lambda_1$ 当且仅当所有权重集中在 $\lambda_1$ 对应的特征向量上，即 $x$ 属于 $\lambda_1$ 的特征子空间；$\lambda_n$ 同理。中间特征值一般不能写成单个 $R(x)$ 的极值。

Courant–Fischer（min-max 形式）：对 $k=1,\dots,n$，$$\lambda_k=\min_{\dim S=k}\ \max_{0\ne x\in S}R(x).$$ 证明：取 $S_0=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_k\}$，对 $x\in S_0$ 有 $R(x)\le\lambda_k$，故 $\max_{S_0}R\le\lambda_k$，从而 $\min_S\max_SR\le\lambda_k$。反向，任取 $k$ 维子空间 $S$，令 $T=\operatorname{span}\{u_k,\dots,u_n\}$，$\dim T=n-k+1$。因 $\dim S+\dim T=n+1>n$，存在 $0\ne x\in S\cap T$；写 $x=\sum_{i=k}^{n}c_iu_i$，得 $R(x)\ge\lambda_k$，故 $\max_SR\ge\lambda_k$，对 $S$ 取极小得 $\min_S\max_SR\ge\lambda_k$。两端合并即得。极值在单位球面上可达，因为 $R$ 连续。

对偶（max-min）形式：$$\lambda_k=\max_{\dim T=n-k+1}\ \min_{0\ne x\in T}R(x).$$ 取 $T_0=\operatorname{span}\{u_k,\dots,u_n\}$，对 $x\in T_0$ 有 $R(x)\ge\lambda_k$，故 $\min_{T_0}R\ge\lambda_k$，从而 $\max_T\min_TR\ge\lambda_k$。反向，任取 $\dim T=n-k+1$ 的子空间，令 $S=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_k\}$；由 $\dim S+\dim T=n+1>n$ 可取 $0\ne x\in S\cap T$，则 $R(x)\le\lambda_k$，故 $\min_TR\le\lambda_k$，对 $T$ 取上确界得 $\max_T\min_TR\le\lambda_k$。两种形式中 $\min$ 与 $\max$ 的次序、子空间维数都不能互换。

驻点刻画：在约束 $\|x\|=1$ 下，$R(x)=x^{H}Ax$。实对称情形（Hermitian 情形把转置换成共轭转置，结论相同） $$\nabla R(x)=\frac{2(Ax-R(x)x)}{x^{T}x}.$$ 令梯度为零（等价于用 Lagrange 乘子处理约束 $\|x\|^2=1$）得 $Ax=R(x)x$，即 $x$ 是 $A$ 的特征向量，驻值就是相应特征值。反过来，每个单位特征向量都满足该方程，故约束驻点恰为特征向量。这解释了第 2 步的端点极值：它们同时也是驻点。

应用（Cauchy 交错）：设 $B$ 是 $A$ 的 $n-1$ 阶主子阵（例如删去最后一行与最后一列），特征值为 $\mu_1\le\cdots\le\mu_{n-1}$。记 $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ 或 $\mathbb{C}$；把 $\mathbb{K}^{n-1}$ 的向量 $\tilde x$ 嵌入 $\mathbb{K}^n$ 为 $(\tilde x,0)$，则 $R_A(\tilde x)=R_B(\tilde x)$。对任意 $k$ 维 $S\subset\mathbb{K}^{n-1}$，由 $\lambda_k$ 的极小极大性，$\lambda_k(A)\le\max_{x\in S}R_A(x)=\max_{x\in S}R_B(x)$；对 $S$ 取极小得 $\lambda_k(A)\le\mu_k(B)$。另一方面取 $S=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_{k+1}\}$，则 $\dim(S\cap\mathbb{K}^{n-1})\ge k$，且在 $S$ 上 $R_A\le\lambda_{k+1}(A)$，于其中取 $k$ 维子空间即得 $\mu_k(B)\le\lambda_{k+1}(A)$。合并得 $$\lambda_k(A)\le\mu_k(B)\le\lambda_{k+1}(A),\qquad k=1,\dots,n-1.$$ 以上证明的是 $n-1$ 阶主子阵。对一般 $m$ 阶主子阵，可对补空间维数归纳（或反复使用 $n-1$ 阶情形），得到 $$\lambda_k(A)\le\mu_k(B)\le\lambda_{k+n-m}(A),\qquad k=1,\dots,m.$$
en: Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be Hermitian ($A^{H}=A$) with eigenvalues in increasing order $\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n$, and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $u_1,\dots,u_n$: $Au_i=\lambda_iu_i$, $u_i^{H}u_j=\delta_{ij}$. For $x\ne0$ define the Rayleigh quotient $$R(x)=\frac{x^{H}Ax}{x^{H}x}.$$ Writing $x=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_iu_i$ gives $x^{H}Ax=\sum_i\lambda_i|c_i|^2$ and $x^{H}x=\sum_i|c_i|^2$, hence $$R(x)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i|c_i|^2}{\sum_i|c_i|^2}.$$ This is a weighted average of the eigenvalues with weights $|c_i|^2$; in particular it is real, and $R(cx)=R(x)$ for $c\ne0$.

The weighted-average formula immediately gives $\lambda_1\le R(x)\le\lambda_n$. Taking $x=u_1$ gives $R=\lambda_1$, and $x=u_n$ gives $R=\lambda_n$; therefore $$\lambda_1=\min_{x\ne0}R(x),\qquad \lambda_n=\max_{x\ne0}R(x).$$ Equality conditions also follow: $R(x)=\lambda_1$ iff all weight is concentrated on eigenvectors for $\lambda_1$, i.e. $x$ lies in the $\lambda_1$-eigenspace; similarly for $\lambda_n$. An intermediate eigenvalue generally cannot be written as an extremum of $R$ over single vectors.

Courant–Fischer (min–max form): for $k=1,\dots,n$, $$\lambda_k=\min_{\dim S=k}\ \max_{0\ne x\in S}R(x).$$ Proof: take $S_0=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_k\}$. For $x\in S_0$, $R(x)\le\lambda_k$, so $\max_{S_0}R\le\lambda_k$ and hence $\min_S\max_SR\le\lambda_k$. Conversely, for any $k$-dimensional $S$, let $T=\operatorname{span}\{u_k,\dots,u_n\}$, of dimension $n-k+1$. Since $\dim S+\dim T=n+1>n$, there is $0\ne x\in S\cap T$; writing $x=\sum_{i=k}^{n}c_iu_i$ gives $R(x)\ge\lambda_k$, so $\max_SR\ge\lambda_k$, and taking the minimum over $S$ yields $\min_S\max_SR\ge\lambda_k$. The two inequalities coincide. The extrema are attained because $R$ is continuous on the unit sphere.

Dual (max–min) form: $$\lambda_k=\max_{\dim T=n-k+1}\ \min_{0\ne x\in T}R(x).$$ Take $T_0=\operatorname{span}\{u_k,\dots,u_n\}$. For $x\in T_0$, $R(x)\ge\lambda_k$, so $\min_{T_0}R\ge\lambda_k$ and hence $\max_T\min_TR\ge\lambda_k$. Conversely, for any $T$ of dimension $n-k+1$, let $S=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_k\}$. Since $\dim S+\dim T=n+1>n$, choose $0\ne x\in S\cap T$; then $R(x)\le\lambda_k$, so $\min_TR\le\lambda_k$, and taking the supremum over $T$ gives $\max_T\min_TR\le\lambda_k$. In both forms neither the order of min and max nor the subspace dimensions may be interchanged.

Stationary points: on the constraint $\|x\|=1$ we have $R(x)=x^{H}Ax$. In the real symmetric case (for the Hermitian case replace the transpose by the conjugate transpose; the conclusion is the same), $$\nabla R(x)=\frac{2(Ax-R(x)x)}{x^{T}x}.$$ Setting the gradient to zero (equivalently, applying a Lagrange multiplier to $\|x\|^2=1$) gives $Ax=R(x)x$, so $x$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the stationary value is the corresponding eigenvalue. Conversely, every unit eigenvector satisfies this equation, so the constrained stationary points are exactly the eigenvectors. This explains why the endpoint extrema in Step 2 are also stationary points.

Application (Cauchy interlacing): let $B$ be an $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ principal submatrix of $A$ (for instance, delete the last row and column), with eigenvalues $\mu_1\le\cdots\le\mu_{n-1}$. Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$; embed $\tilde x\in\mathbb{K}^{n-1}$ as $(\tilde x,0)\in\mathbb{K}^n$; then $R_A(\tilde x)=R_B(\tilde x)$. For every $k$-dimensional $S\subset\mathbb{K}^{n-1}$, the min–max characterization gives $\lambda_k(A)\le\max_{x\in S}R_A(x)=\max_{x\in S}R_B(x)$; taking the minimum over $S$ yields $\lambda_k(A)\le\mu_k(B)$. Conversely, take $S=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_{k+1}\}$; then $\dim(S\cap\mathbb{K}^{n-1})\ge k$, and on $S$ we have $R_A\le\lambda_{k+1}(A)$, so choosing a $k$-dimensional subspace of the intersection gives $\mu_k(B)\le\lambda_{k+1}(A)$. Hence $$\lambda_k(A)\le\mu_k(B)\le\lambda_{k+1}(A),\qquad k=1,\dots,n-1.$$ This proves the case of an $(n-1)$-st order principal submatrix. For a general $m$-th order principal submatrix, induct on the codimension (or iterate the $(n-1)$ case) to obtain $$\lambda_k(A)\le\mu_k(B)\le\lambda_{k+n-m}(A),\qquad k=1,\dots,m.$$

zh: 设 $V$ 是域 $K$ 上的 $n$ 维线性空间，$e_1,\dots,e_n$ 是一组基。线性函数 $f:V\to K$ 的全体构成对偶空间 $V^*=\mathcal{L}(V,K)$。定义 $\varepsilon_i\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_je_j\right)=a_i$，则 $\varepsilon_i$ 线性且 $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$。对任意 $f\in V^*$，$f(\alpha)=\sum_i a_if(e_i)$，故 $f=\sum_i f(e_i)\varepsilon_i$，说明 $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ 张成 $V^*$；若 $\sum_i c_i\varepsilon_i=0$，代入 $e_j$ 得 $c_j=0$，说明它们线性无关。因此 $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ 是 $V^*$ 的基（对偶基），$\dim V^*=n$。

对偶基依赖原基的选取，不能把 $V$ 与 $V^*$ 自然等同。若新基 $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$（矩阵 $P=(p_{ij})$ 可逆），设对偶基 $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k$，则由 $$\begin{aligned}\varepsilon'_i(e'_j)&=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k(e'_j)\\&=\sum_k a_{ik}p_{kj}=(AP)_{ij}=\delta_{ij}.\end{aligned}$$ 得 $A=P^{-1}$，即 $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k(P^{-1})_{ik}\varepsilon_k$。原基按 $P$ 变换，对偶基按 $P^{-1}$ 反向变换；这正是「没有自然同构」的具体含义。

双对偶与自然嵌入：定义 $\iota:V\to V^{**}$，$\iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha)$。它不依赖任何基，且是线性的。若 $\iota(\alpha)=0$，则对所有 $f\in V^*$ 有 $f(\alpha)=0$；当 $\alpha\ne0$ 时，把 $\alpha$ 扩充为基，并令 $f(\alpha)=1$、其余基向量映为 $0$，得到 $f(\alpha)=1$，矛盾，故 $\alpha=0$，$\iota$ 单射。有限维时 $\dim V^{**}=\dim V^*=\dim V$，单射的线性映射在等维空间之间必为满射，故 $\iota$ 是同构；无限维时 $\iota(V)$ 只是 $V^{**}$ 的真子集（这是无限维的标准结论），「有限维」条件不能省。

零化子：对子空间 $S\le V$，定义 $$S^{\circ}=\{f\in V^*: f(s)=0,\ \forall s\in S\}.$$ 取 $S$ 的基 $e_1,\dots,e_k$ 并扩充为 $V$ 的基 $e_1,\dots,e_n$，对偶基为 $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$。若 $f=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\varepsilon_i$，则 $f(e_j)=a_j$（$j\le k$），故 $f\in S^{\circ}\iff a_1=\cdots=a_k=0$，即 $S^{\circ}=\operatorname{span}\{\varepsilon_{k+1},\dots,\varepsilon_n\}$。因此 $$\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=k+(n-k)=n=\dim V.$$

双线性型：$B:V\times V\to K$ 对两个变量分别线性。取基 $e_1,\dots,e_n$，令 $A=(B(e_i,e_j))$。若 $x=\sum_i x_ie_i$、$y=\sum_j y_je_j$，则由双线性 $$B(x,y)=\sum_{i,j}x_iy_jB(e_i,e_j)=x^{T}Ay.$$ 换基 $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$ 时坐标满足 $x=Px'$、$y=Py'$，故 $$B(x,y)=(x')^{T}(P^{T}AP)y',$$ 即矩阵按合同 $A\mapsto P^{T}AP$ 变换。$B$ 对称（$B(x,y)=B(y,x)$）当且仅当 $A^{T}=A$；合同保持秩，但不保持特征值。

对称双线性型与二次型：令 $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$。直接展开得 $$Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha).$$ 当 $B$ 对称时右边为 $2B(\alpha,\beta)$，故当域的特征不等于 $2$ 时 $$B(\alpha,\beta)=\frac12\big(Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)\big),$$ 二次型与对称双线性型互相唯一决定。特征不等于 $2$ 时，若 $B$ 反对称，则 $B(\alpha,\alpha)=0$、$Q\equiv0$，极化恒等式只恢复对称部分 $\frac12(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha))$；特征 $2$ 时不能除以 $2$，上述对应失效。
en: Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over $K$ with basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$. The set of all linear functionals $f:V\to K$ forms the dual space $V^*=\mathcal{L}(V,K)$. Define $\varepsilon_i(\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_je_j)=a_i$; then $\varepsilon_i$ is linear and $\varepsilon_i(e_j)=\delta_{ij}$. For any $f\in V^*$, $f(\alpha)=\sum_i a_if(e_i)$, so $f=\sum_i f(e_i)\varepsilon_i$ and the $\varepsilon_i$ span $V^*$. If $\sum_i c_i\varepsilon_i=0$, evaluating at $e_j$ gives $c_j=0$, so they are independent. Hence $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ is a basis of $V^*$ (the dual basis), and $\dim V^*=n$.

The dual basis depends on the choice of basis, so $V$ and $V^*$ cannot be naturally identified. If a new basis is $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$ with $P=(p_{ij})$ invertible, and $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k$, then $$\varepsilon'_i(e'_j)=\sum_k a_{ik}\varepsilon_k\left(\sum_l p_{lj}e_l\right)=\sum_k a_{ik}p_{kj}=(AP)_{ij}=\delta_{ij},$$ so $A=P^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon'_i=\sum_k(P^{-1})_{ik}\varepsilon_k$. The original basis changes by $P$, while the dual basis changes by $P^{-1}$ in the opposite direction; this is the concrete meaning of 'no natural isomorphism'.

Double dual and canonical embedding: define $\iota:V\to V^{**}$ by $\iota(\alpha)(f)=f(\alpha)$. It uses no basis and is linear. If $\iota(\alpha)=0$, then $f(\alpha)=0$ for every $f\in V^*$. If $\alpha\ne0$, extend $\alpha$ to a basis and define $f$ to be $1$ on $\alpha$ and $0$ on the other basis vectors, giving $f(\alpha)=1$, a contradiction. Hence $\alpha=0$ and $\iota$ is injective. In finite dimension $\dim V^{**}=\dim V^*=\dim V$, so an injective linear map between spaces of equal dimension is surjective, and $\iota$ is an isomorphism. In infinite dimension $\iota(V)$ is a proper subset of $V^{**}$ (a standard infinite-dimensional fact); the finite-dimensional hypothesis cannot be dropped.

Annihilator: for a subspace $S\le V$, define $$S^{\circ}=\{f\in V^*: f(s)=0\ \text{for all }s\in S\}.$$ Choose a basis $e_1,\dots,e_k$ of $S$ and extend it to a basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ of $V$, with dual basis $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$. If $f=\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i\varepsilon_i$, then $f(e_j)=a_j$ for $j\le k$; hence $f\in S^{\circ}$ iff $a_1=\cdots=a_k=0$, i.e. $S^{\circ}=\operatorname{span}\{\varepsilon_{k+1},\dots,\varepsilon_n\}$. Therefore $$\dim S+\dim S^{\circ}=k+(n-k)=n=\dim V.$$

Bilinear forms: a map $B:V\times V\to K$ is bilinear if it is linear in each variable separately. Fix a basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ and let $A=(B(e_i,e_j))$. For $x=\sum_i x_ie_i$ and $y=\sum_j y_je_j$, bilinearity gives $$B(x,y)=\sum_{i,j}x_iy_jB(e_i,e_j)=x^{T}Ay.$$ Under a change of basis $e'_j=\sum_i p_{ij}e_i$ the coordinates satisfy $x=Px'$, $y=Py'$, hence $$B(x,y)=(x')^{T}(P^{T}AP)y',$$ so the matrix transforms by congruence $A\mapsto P^{T}AP$. The form $B$ is symmetric ($B(x,y)=B(y,x)$) iff $A^{T}=A$; congruence preserves rank but not eigenvalues.

Symmetric bilinear forms and quadratic forms: put $Q(\alpha)=B(\alpha,\alpha)$. Direct expansion gives $$Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha).$$ If $B$ is symmetric, the right side is $2B(\alpha,\beta)$, so over a field of characteristic not $2$, $$B(\alpha,\beta)=\frac12\big(Q(\alpha+\beta)-Q(\alpha)-Q(\beta)\big),$$ and the quadratic form and the symmetric bilinear form determine each other uniquely. Over a field of characteristic not $2$, an antisymmetric $B$ satisfies $B(\alpha,\alpha)=0$ and $Q\equiv0$, so polarization recovers only the symmetric part $\frac12(B(\alpha,\beta)+B(\beta,\alpha))$; in characteristic $2$ division by $2$ is impossible and this correspondence fails.

zh: 设 $W\le V$ 是子空间。对 $\alpha\in V$ 定义陪集 $\alpha+W=\{\alpha+w:w\in W\}$，全体陪集记作 $V/W$。陪集相等有判别法：$$\alpha+W=\beta+W\iff\alpha-\beta\in W.$$ 若 $\alpha-\beta=w\in W$，则对任意 $u\in W$，$\alpha+u=\beta+(w+u)\in\beta+W$，且 $w+W=W$，故两陪集相等；反之若相等，由 $\alpha=\alpha+0\in\beta+W$ 得 $\alpha=\beta+w$，即 $\alpha-\beta\in W$。

在 $V/W$ 上定义 $$(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=(\alpha+\beta)+W,\qquad k(\alpha+W)=k\alpha+W.$$ 必须验证良定义：若换代表元 $\alpha'=\alpha+w_1$、$\beta'=\beta+w_2$（$w_1,w_2\in W$），则 $$\alpha'+\beta'=(\alpha+\beta)+(w_1+w_2),\qquad k\alpha'=k\alpha+kw_1,$$ 而 $w_1+w_2\in W$、$kw_1\in W$。由第 1 步，$(\alpha'+\beta')+W=(\alpha+\beta)+W$、$k\alpha'+W=k\alpha+W$，结果与代表元选取无关。

验证线性空间公理：加法结合律与交换律、零元 $0+W=W$、负元 $(-\alpha)+W$ 都从 $V$ 的相应性质逐项继承。例如 $$(\alpha+W)+W=(\alpha+0)+W=\alpha+W.$$ 数乘分配律同样逐项验证：$(k+l)(\alpha+W)=(k+l)\alpha+W=(k\alpha+l\alpha)+W=k(\alpha+W)+l(\alpha+W)$，且 $k(l(\alpha+W))=(kl)(\alpha+W)$、$1(\alpha+W)=\alpha+W$。因运算已良定义，这些等式在陪集层面成立，故 $V/W$ 是 $K$ 上的线性空间。

自然投影 $\pi:V\to V/W$，$\pi(\alpha)=\alpha+W$。由定义 $\pi(\alpha+\beta)=(\alpha+\beta)+W=(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=\pi(\alpha)+\pi(\beta)$，$\pi(k\alpha)=k\pi(\alpha)$，故线性；任意陪集 $\alpha+W$ 等于 $\pi(\alpha)$，故满射。核为 $$\ker\pi=\{\alpha:\alpha+W=W\}=\{\alpha:\alpha\in W\}=W.$$ 对有限维 $V$，秩–零化度定理给出 $\dim V=\dim\ker\pi+\dim\operatorname{Im}\pi=\dim W+\dim(V/W)$，即 $$\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W.$$

第一同构定理：设 $T:V\to Y$ 线性。定义 $$\varphi:V/\ker T\to\operatorname{Im}T,\qquad \varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=T\alpha.$$ 良定义：若 $\alpha+\ker T=\beta+\ker T$，则 $\alpha-\beta\in\ker T$，故 $T\alpha=T\beta$。$\varphi$ 线性：$\varphi((\alpha+\ker T)+(\beta+\ker T))=T(\alpha+\beta)=T\alpha+T\beta$，数乘同理。核为零：$\varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=0\Rightarrow T\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha\in\ker T$，即该陪集是零陪集。满射由值域定义。因此 $V/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T$，取维数得 $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$。

商空间的普遍性质：若 $T:V\to Y$ 线性且 $W\subseteq\ker T$，定义 $\bar T:V/W\to Y$、$\bar T(\alpha+W)=T\alpha$。由 $W\subseteq\ker T$ 知其良定义，且 $T=\bar T\circ\pi$；因 $\pi$ 满射，满足此分解的 $\bar T$ 唯一。取 $W=\ker T$ 就回到第一同构定理。线性方程组的情形：$Ax=b$ 若有解 $x_0$，则解集为 $x_0+\ker A$——两个解之差是齐次解；同时 $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$，商空间把「核的自由度」与「像」分开。
en: Let $W\le V$ be a subspace. For $\alpha\in V$ define the coset $\alpha+W=\{\alpha+w:w\in W\}$; the set of all cosets is denoted $V/W$. Cosets satisfy the equality test $$\alpha+W=\beta+W\iff\alpha-\beta\in W.$$ If $\alpha-\beta=w\in W$, then for every $u\in W$, $\alpha+u=\beta+(w+u)\in\beta+W$, and $w+W=W$, so the cosets coincide. Conversely, if they are equal, then $\alpha=\alpha+0\in\beta+W$, so $\alpha=\beta+w$ and $\alpha-\beta\in W$.

Define on $V/W$ $$(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=(\alpha+\beta)+W,\qquad k(\alpha+W)=k\alpha+W.$$ Well-definedness must be checked: if representatives are changed to $\alpha'=\alpha+w_1$ and $\beta'=\beta+w_2$ with $w_1,w_2\in W$, then $$\alpha'+\beta'=(\alpha+\beta)+(w_1+w_2),\qquad k\alpha'=k\alpha+kw_1,$$ and $w_1+w_2\in W$, $kw_1\in W$. By Step 1, $(\alpha'+\beta')+W=(\alpha+\beta)+W$ and $k\alpha'+W=k\alpha+W$, so the result is independent of the representatives.

Vector-space axioms: associativity and commutativity of addition, the zero element $0+W=W$, and the inverse $-\alpha+W$ are inherited term by term from $V$. For example, $$(\alpha+W)+W=(\alpha+0)+W=\alpha+W.$$ The scalar distributive laws are checked similarly: $(k+l)(\alpha+W)=(k+l)\alpha+W=(k\alpha+l\alpha)+W=k(\alpha+W)+l(\alpha+W)$, and $k(l(\alpha+W))=(kl)(\alpha+W)$, $1(\alpha+W)=\alpha+W$. Since the operations are well defined, these identities hold at the level of cosets, so $V/W$ is a vector space over $K$.

The natural projection $\pi:V\to V/W$, $\pi(\alpha)=\alpha+W$, is linear: $\pi(\alpha+\beta)=(\alpha+\beta)+W=(\alpha+W)+(\beta+W)=\pi(\alpha)+\pi(\beta)$, and $\pi(k\alpha)=k\pi(\alpha)$; it is surjective because every coset is $\pi(\alpha)$. Its kernel is $$\ker\pi=\{\alpha:\alpha+W=W\}=\{\alpha:\alpha\in W\}=W.$$ For finite-dimensional $V$, rank–nullity gives $\dim V=\dim\ker\pi+\dim\operatorname{Im}\pi=\dim W+\dim(V/W)$, hence $$\dim(V/W)=\dim V-\dim W.$$

First isomorphism theorem: let $T:V\to Y$ be linear. Define $$\varphi:V/\ker T\to\operatorname{Im}T,\qquad \varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=T\alpha.$$ It is well defined: if $\alpha+\ker T=\beta+\ker T$, then $\alpha-\beta\in\ker T$, so $T\alpha=T\beta$. It is linear, since $\varphi((\alpha+\ker T)+(\beta+\ker T))=T(\alpha+\beta)=T\alpha+T\beta$, and similarly for scalars. Its kernel is zero: $\varphi(\alpha+\ker T)=0$ implies $T\alpha=0$, so $\alpha\in\ker T$ and the coset is the zero coset. It is surjective onto its codomain by definition. Therefore $V/\ker T\cong\operatorname{Im}T$, and taking dimensions gives $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{Im}T$.

Universal property of the quotient: if $T:V\to Y$ is linear and $W\subseteq\ker T$, define $\bar T:V/W\to Y$ by $\bar T(\alpha+W)=T\alpha$. The inclusion $W\subseteq\ker T$ makes it well defined, and $T=\bar T\circ\pi$; since $\pi$ is surjective, such a $\bar T$ is unique. Taking $W=\ker T$ recovers the first isomorphism theorem. For linear systems, if $Ax=b$ has a solution $x_0$, its solution set is $x_0+\ker A$—two solutions differ by a homogeneous solution—and $K^n/\ker A\cong\operatorname{Im}A$ separates the degrees of freedom in the kernel from the image.

zh: 构造：先取以集合 $V\times W$ 为基的自由向量空间 $F$，即把每个形式符号 $(\alpha,\beta)$ 当作基向量；再令 $R$ 为所有下列关系张成的子空间：$$\begin{aligned}&(k\alpha,\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha,k\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha_1+\alpha_2,\beta)-(\alpha_1,\beta)-(\alpha_2,\beta),\\&(\alpha,\beta_1+\beta_2)-(\alpha,\beta_1)-(\alpha,\beta_2).\end{aligned}$$ 定义 $V\otimes W=F/R$，并记 $\alpha\otimes\beta=(\alpha,\beta)+R$。由商空间构造，$\otimes$ 对两个变量分别线性；构造中没有加入 $\alpha\otimes\beta=\beta\otimes\alpha$ 的关系，所以二者一般不等。

万有性质：设 $B:V\times W\to U$ 双线性。在 $F$ 上定义线性映射 $\Phi$，使基向量 $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto B(\alpha,\beta)$。因 $B$ 双线性，$\Phi$ 在 $R$ 的每个生成元上取零，故诱导出线性映射 $\tilde B:V\otimes W\to U$，满足 $$\tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta).$$ 若另有 $\tilde B'$ 满足同样条件，则二者在张成 $V\otimes W$ 的纯张量上一致，故 $\tilde B'=\tilde B$，唯一性成立。反之，任一线性 $\tilde B$ 与 $\otimes$ 复合给出双线性映射，于是双线性映射与线性映射一一对应。

纯张量张成：由构造，$V\otimes W$ 中每个元素都是有限个基向量 $(\alpha,\beta)$ 的像的线性组合，即有限和 $\sum_{r=1}^{N}c_r\,\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r$。它一般不是「两个向量的乘积」，而是纯张量的有限和。取 $V$ 的基 $e_1,\dots,e_m$ 与 $W$ 的基 $f_1,\dots,f_n$，把 $\alpha_r=\sum_i a_{ir}e_i$、$\beta_r=\sum_j b_{jr}f_j$ 代入并用双线性，得 $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{r}c_r\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r&=\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}\,e_i\otimes f_j,\\C_{ij}&=\sum_{r}c_ra_{ir}b_{jr}.\end{aligned}$$ 故 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 张成 $V\otimes W$。

证明 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 线性无关。对每对 $(i_0,j_0)$，定义双线性型 $B_{i_0j_0}(\alpha,\beta)=a_{i_0}b_{j_0}$，其中 $\alpha=\sum_i a_ie_i$、$\beta=\sum_j b_jf_j$。由万有性质得到线性函数 $\varphi_{i_0j_0}:V\otimes W\to K$，满足 $$\varphi_{i_0j_0}(e_i\otimes f_j)=\delta_{ii_0}\delta_{jj_0}.$$ 若 $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j=0$，两边作用 $\varphi_{i_0j_0}$ 得 $c_{i_0j_0}=0$。所有系数为零，故 $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ 线性无关。结合第 3 步，它是基，于是 $$\dim(V\otimes W)=mn=\dim V\cdot\dim W.$$

纯张量的判别：若 $\alpha\ne0$、$\beta\ne0$，分别取以 $\alpha$ 为第一个基向量的 $V$ 的基、以 $\beta$ 为第一个基向量的 $W$ 的基，则 $\alpha\otimes\beta=e_1\otimes f_1$，是基元素，故不为零。反之，若某一因子为 $0$，双线性给出 $\alpha\otimes\beta=0$。因此对向量空间 $$\alpha\otimes\beta=0\iff\alpha=0\ \text{或}\ \beta=0.$$ 固定基后，纯张量 $\alpha\otimes\beta$ 的系数矩阵为外积 $\alpha\beta^{T}$，两因子非零时秩为 $1$；反之秩一矩阵都可写成外积。故 $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$ 时存在非纯张量，例如 $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$ 的系数矩阵 $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ 秩为 $2$。

具体同构：$\mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$，由 $e_i\otimes f_j\mapsto E_{ij}$ 线性延拓，其中 $E_{ij}$ 是 $(i,j)$ 位置为 $1$、其余为 $0$ 的矩阵。于是 $\alpha\otimes\beta\mapsto\alpha\beta^{T}$（列乘行），其秩为 $1$；一般张量 $\sum c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j$ 对应矩阵 $(c_{ij})$。两边维数都是 $mn$，与第 4 步一致。有限维时还有 $V^*\otimes W\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$，对应 $f\otimes\beta\mapsto(\alpha\mapsto f(\alpha)\beta)$；这说明线性映射本身也可以写成张量。
en: Construction: first take the free vector space $F$ on the set $V\times W$, treating each formal symbol $(\alpha,\beta)$ as a basis vector; let $R$ be the subspace spanned by all relations $$\begin{aligned}&(k\alpha,\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha,k\beta)-k(\alpha,\beta),\\&(\alpha_1+\alpha_2,\beta)-(\alpha_1,\beta)-(\alpha_2,\beta),\\&(\alpha,\beta_1+\beta_2)-(\alpha,\beta_1)-(\alpha,\beta_2).\end{aligned}$$ Define $V\otimes W=F/R$ and write $\alpha\otimes\beta=(\alpha,\beta)+R$. By the quotient construction, $\otimes$ is linear in each variable; no relation $\alpha\otimes\beta=\beta\otimes\alpha$ is imposed, so the two are generally unequal.

Universal property: let $B:V\times W\to U$ be bilinear. Define a linear map $\Phi$ on $F$ by sending each basis vector $(\alpha,\beta)$ to $B(\alpha,\beta)$. Because $B$ is bilinear, $\Phi$ vanishes on every generator of $R$, so it induces a linear map $\tilde B:V\otimes W\to U$ satisfying $$\tilde B(\alpha\otimes\beta)=B(\alpha,\beta).$$ If another $\tilde B'$ satisfies the same condition, then $\tilde B'=\tilde B$ on the pure tensors, which span $V\otimes W$, so $\tilde B'=\tilde B$; uniqueness holds. Conversely, any linear $\tilde B$ composed with $\otimes$ gives a bilinear map, so bilinear maps and linear maps correspond one-to-one.

Pure tensors span: by construction every element of $V\otimes W$ is a linear combination of the images of finitely many basis vectors $(\alpha,\beta)$, i.e. a finite sum $\sum_{r=1}^{N}c_r\,\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r$. It is not in general a single product of two vectors, but a finite sum of pure tensors. Take bases $e_1,\dots,e_m$ of $V$ and $f_1,\dots,f_n$ of $W$, write $\alpha_r=\sum_i a_{ir}e_i$ and $\beta_r=\sum_j b_{jr}f_j$, and use bilinearity: $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{r}c_r\alpha_r\otimes\beta_r&=\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}\,e_i\otimes f_j,\\C_{ij}&=\sum_{r}c_ra_{ir}b_{jr}.\end{aligned}$$ Hence $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$ spans $V\otimes W$.

Independence of $\{e_i\otimes f_j\}$: for each pair $(i_0,j_0)$ define the bilinear form $B_{i_0j_0}(\alpha,\beta)=a_{i_0}b_{j_0}$, where $\alpha=\sum_i a_ie_i$ and $\beta=\sum_j b_jf_j$. The universal property gives a linear functional $\varphi_{i_0j_0}:V\otimes W\to K$ with $$\varphi_{i_0j_0}(e_i\otimes f_j)=\delta_{ii_0}\delta_{jj_0}.$$ If $\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j=0$, applying $\varphi_{i_0j_0}$ gives $c_{i_0j_0}=0$. All coefficients vanish, so the set is linearly independent. Together with Step 3 it is a basis, and $$\dim(V\otimes W)=mn=\dim V\cdot\dim W.$$

Criterion for pure tensors: if $\alpha\ne0$ and $\beta\ne0$, choose a basis of $V$ whose first vector is $\alpha$ and a basis of $W$ whose first vector is $\beta$; then $\alpha\otimes\beta=e_1\otimes f_1$, a nonzero basis element. Conversely, if one factor is $0$, bilinearity gives $\alpha\otimes\beta=0$. Thus for vector spaces $$\alpha\otimes\beta=0\iff\alpha=0\ \text{or}\ \beta=0.$$ In a fixed basis, a pure tensor $\alpha\otimes\beta$ has coefficient matrix the outer product $\alpha\beta^{T}$, of rank $1$ when both factors are nonzero; conversely every rank-one matrix is such an outer product. Hence non-pure tensors exist when $\dim V,\dim W\ge2$: for example $e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1$ has coefficient matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, of rank $2$.

Concrete isomorphism: $\mathbb{R}^m\otimes\mathbb{R}^n\cong M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$, determined by $e_i\otimes f_j\mapsto E_{ij}$, where $E_{ij}$ has a $1$ in position $(i,j)$ and zeros elsewhere. Then $\alpha\otimes\beta\mapsto\alpha\beta^{T}$ (column times row), which has rank one; a general tensor $\sum c_{ij}e_i\otimes f_j$ corresponds to the matrix $(c_{ij})$. Both sides have dimension $mn$, consistent with Step 4. In finite dimension there is also $V^*\otimes W\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, given by $f\otimes\beta\mapsto(\alpha\mapsto f(\alpha)\beta)$; this shows that linear maps themselves can be written as tensors.
